label: London Courrier: Engelsk-Amiralitets konflikt
description:
Stockholm, No. 22.
January 28th, 1780, Friday
Daily News,
or:
All-Comprehensive Daily.
Wednesday, January 26th, with snowfall and high barometer reading of 25.97. Afternoon temperature was 7 degrees, evening temperature 4 degrees, and Thursday morning temperature 3 degrees below freezing. The weather was poor.
Foreign News:
London, January 4th. Yesterday a courier arrived from our Admiral Fielding with dispatches that caused much attention; they contained news of Mr. Fielding's encounter on the night of December 31st against an enemy fleet consisting of three warships and sixty merchant ships. He had sent his officers to compliment the Dutch admiral, asked what he intended, and inquired about the condition of the merchant ships according to their instructions; the Dutch admiral replied that his warships were bound for the West Indies while the merchant ships would go to various French ports. He also mentioned that they carried corn and linseed but lacked shipwrights or carpenters, and he could not allow any inspection as per his instructions. Mr. Fielding responded: If you think differently tomorrow, I will have to take action. Both fleets lay at anchor opposite each other overnight, but the next day, January 1st, Mr. Fielding sent a more urgent message with news that he intended to inspect the merchant ships; they had to comply whatever happened. At ten o'clock, Mr. Fielding ordered his armed sloops to depart from their warships, on which the Dutch admiral took a canoe. Mr. Fielding then fired a shot from his ship, which was returned by the entire crew of the Dutch admiral's vessel; two English ships opened fire on the Dutch admiral and the other ships hoisted their flags. Mr. Fielding summoned him to accept an apology with the condition that he could continue his journey once inspection was over; but the Dutch admiral replied that he would share the same fate as his convoy unless the English admiral requested it in a Christian manner, then he would comply; this happened and was carried out immediately, and the Dutch fleet saluted the English with thirteen shots. Mr. Fielding responded with an equal number of shots, and both fleets arrived at Spithead on December 2nd evening. The court has sent an urgent dispatch to the Dutch ambassador Graf Welderen regarding this incident; it is believed that he was killed in the process. A courier left for Riddor Nork in The Hague tonight. Likewise, Graf Welderen had a lengthy conference with Lord Stormond as soon as she learned of this event and subsequently dispatched another courier to The Hague.
Under these trying circumstances, which are daily worsening, peace is still spoken about. Dispatches from the court on December 31st from Paris contain similar propositions made by Mr. Franklin in Congress's name.
The end of the note regarding upbringing theory (See Gardbag-Bladet).
It has been noticed that this knowledge is not a benefit but rather a burden, as it cannot be brought without heart satisfaction. What does it mean to live and constantly be plagued with all kinds of desires? It can be said that through pleasant feelings such desires are driven away and some kind of peace is obtained. But this art is not long-lasting; when the emotions subside, the frustration becomes even more intense; and the body suffers from this in a greater way. It has been concluded that those who wish to make human hearts happy must eliminate all causes which cause anxiety and the associated plagues. It was not so dark as to expose the causes which so strongly create and torment the soul. It is soon seen that such understanding and will's errors, which are committed by the will itself, form the first part of man's dissatisfaction. Therefore it has been concluded: Man must be fully enlightened and satisfied; his mind should be illuminated and his will brought into order. This means a person who wishes to live happily must be virtuous. And if she is to be virtuous, her understanding must be as well refined and enlightened so that the necessities of both desires and will are met.
All wise men who have established schools in order to teach wisdom and reason, have directed all their efforts and thoughts towards this end; their disputes, which more often than not arise from their statements, are for the most part edifying.

Utländska Nyheter:
London den 4 Januarii. I går anlände en Courir tik Amiralitetet från våre Chef d'Esquader Fiel ding, hvars medbragte depescher härstades föranlätit mycket upmärksamhet; De innehåla at H:r. Fielsoing den 31 December mot aftenen sköt vä en Holländske Flotta, bestäende af 3 Krigs-Skepp och 60 Handels-Skepp. Han låt skratt igenom en affärd Officerare complimentera den Holländske Amiralen, eftersfrågade hvad han ämnade sig, och åskundade tilstand at, enligt sin Instruction, så visstera Handels-Skeppen; Holländska Amiralen svarade höglit: At hans Krigs-Skepp ånade sig till Westindien och Handels-Skeppen til åtskillige Franziske hamnar, han sadé tillika at de innehade Jörn och Linföd, men hwarken Skepswrice eller Tågwerk, och at han, enligt sin Instruction, icke kunde tilläta någon visitation. H:r. Fielding låt gifwa det svar: Ar han förmodade det Amiralen följande dagen torde tänka annorlunda. Båda Flottorne blewo ligande wid hwarandra, natten öfver, men dagen därva, eller den 1 Jan. nickade H:r. Fielding et alswariammare bud, med underrättelse at han årnade visitera Handels-Skeppen, därfat måtte och hånda hvad som hälst. Klockan 10 låt H:r. Fielding afgå frän hwarje af sina Skepp bewapnade Slupar, på hwilka den Holländske Amiralen tokade et Canoasvott. H:r. Fielding lohade därpå et dylikt skott frän sitt Skepp, som af Holländske Amiralen besvarades med hela laget, hwarpå 2:ne Engelske Skepp losade sina lag på Holländske Amiralen, som strakt tillika med de öfrige des Skepp strko Flaggan. H:r. Fielding annlodade honom at åtete uvsäktes den med yttrande, at han kunde forsjärta sin reisa, så snart visitationen wore förbr; men Holländske Amiralen svarade at han wille dela lika öde med sin Convoj och icke stillas ifrån den samma, dock om Engelske Amiralen kristeligt begärte at han skulle bika sin Flagg, så ville han göra det; Detta skedde och werkeligers strakt, och den Holländske Flottan saluterede den Engelske med 13 skott. H:r. Fielding swarade med lika många skott, och båda Esquadrerne anlände til Spithead den 2 December om aftenon. Hofvet har gifvit Holländske Ambassadeuren Grefwe Welderen en omsändelig undermätteser om denne affalset; hwaravsh inges man bliswit dödad. En Courie är och afgången denna aften til Riddören Nork i Haag; Likaledes har Grefswé Welderen, så snart hon årforit denne händelse, haft en läng conference med wär Stats-Secreter Lord Stormond och skrat däræfter åswen afsendt en Courie til Haag. Under dese för os brydsamme omständigheter, som dageligen synas fördöka sig, talas dock om fred. Depescher, som Hofvet den 31 Decemb. fält frän Paris, stola innehålla dylika propositioner, hwilka H:r. Franklin gjordt i Congresens namn.
Slut af Anmärkningen wid Upfostringssläran. (Se Gårdbags-Bladet.)
De flokaste uppå denna jorden hafwa snart märkt, at detta lätvet ej är någon näfva, utan en börda nge det tilbringas utan hjärtaks tilfridsställelse. Hvad betyder det at lefwa, och ständigt plågad samt af allahanda begärleter hit och dit drifwen warda. Det går an, at igenom angenäma känslor fördrifswa sådans olust, och förskaffa sig en slags ro. Men denna konst warar ei länge. Når känslorna bliswå slappa, så raser sedan ledsnaden mera än föikut; och kroppen warder öfwen härigenom mera förstwagad och uendtt. Man har widare förnuftigt slutadt, at de som welat göra människo-hjärtat roligt, måste undanrödja alla de orsaker, hwaraf war oro och de laster som därmed åro förbundne plågar slyta.* Det var ej så svart at raka uppå de orsaker, hwilka så starkt skafa och qwälja wär sjål. Når femt snart, at så walt förståndets oivishet och wills farelser, som willans begår och böielser, hade första delen i alt människons misknöje. Man gjorde därfore den slutsæ: Skall människan bliswå fullt falks och tilfridsställd, så måtte dess anda uplyst och dess willa k ordning bringas. Det wil så mycket säga, en människa, som wil lefwa lyckligt måste vara dygig. Och skall hon bliswå dygig måste hennes förstånd så wida renat och uplyst bliswå, som til begärens o h willans kyrande de nöddigt.
